benefits: Size: Medium (4). +6 Strength, +3 Dexterity, +2 Bow, Endurance, and Pugilism Skills, and +2 DR. Each floor you receive a coupon for one free training at a Weapon Training Guild; the race has little innate magical ability.
name: Amazonian
prerequisites: This limited Race is only available to crawlers who have at least one Strength or Dexterity-based Skill at Rank 5+

benefits: Size: Medium (4). +5 Dexterity, +3 Web Spell which costs half the normal Mana to cast, and +2 Climbing, Perception, and Performance (with a stringed instrument specialty) Skills. You have an innate Climb Move equal to your normal Move value, without needing Checks unless under duress.
name: Arachnid

benefits: Size: Small (2); Animal. +4 Dexterity, +2 Constitution, +1 Charisma, -3 Strength, +3 Cat-like Reflexes, and +2 Slice Attack Skill. You can see in total darkness, have Advantage on Cat-like Reflexes Skill Checks, and Nine Lives lets you take half damage from the first 9 attacks each day, but you take double damage from Dogs and Beasts.
name: Cat
prerequisites: This limited Race is only available to crawlers who are already a Cat

benefits: Size: Medium (4). +3 Dexterity and Charisma, -2 Constitution, and +2 Cat-like Reflexes, Good First Impression, Light on your Feet, and Slice Attack Skills. Your Slice Attacks may add your Cha Mod to damage instead of Str. Once per day, Toxoplasma G. gives your allies Rank 5 Catcher Skill (and the +5 DR Upgrade) for one round to protect only you, and those who do gain 1 AI Favor; you make Charisma-based Skill Checks with Disadvantage when dealing with felines other than Cat Girls/Boys.
name: Cat Girl/Cat Boy

benefits: Size: Medium (4). +5 Dexterity, +3 Strength and Constitution, -2 Charisma, and +3 Ambush and Creepy Chains (Club) Skills. Creepy Chains lets you use any chain as a weapon (Club Weapon Skill, 10ft range) and lengthen or shorten any chain by 50% once per scene. A foe touching you with bare skin takes 1d4+F Acid; you need not breathe, are vulnerable to Holy damage, and cannot worship a deity.
name: Changbi Demon

benefits: Size: Large (5). +3 Charisma, +2 Intelligence, +2 Ambush and Deception Skills, and +1 Escape Artist Skill, with Advantage on Deception Skill Checks when no talking is needed. By touching a member of another Race you can build a library of Races to shapeshift into as an Action (Unopposed Deception Skill Check), gaining that Race's bonuses other than statistics and Skills while shifted. Changelings can't touch mimics-type creatures. Changelings gain free access to organizations and producers by impersonating other crawlers and Syndicate celebrities, but can only use those relevant to the currently shifted individual. While shapeshifted into another Race, these changes are conveyed to World Dungeon systems, including information on viewers' HUDs, mini-maps, and other systems.
name: Changeling

benefits: Size: Large (5). +4 Strength, +3 Constitution, and +2 Pugilism and Powerful Strike Skills. You roll Intimidate Skill Checks with Advantage when physically menacing someone in person, gain +3 DR Buff, and +1 Buff for all Skill Checks for 1 hour after eating a full meal. While Fatigued, you roll all Charisma-based Checks with Disadvantage.
name: Crocodilian

benefits: Size: Unchanged, but size changes when shifting. +4 Constitution, +3 Strength, +1 Deception and Endurance Skills, and +2 DR. You determine maximum weight to lift based on Constitution instead of Strength, have Advantage on Escape Artist Skill Checks (even while Held or watched), and once per scene as an Action can incorporate a held weapon into your mass for additional damage equal to your Con Mod (it can't be disarmed). Shape-Changing as an Action lets you transform into any shape of comparable mass, costing 1 Health Bar slot per change, with an Unopposed Deception Skill Check to resemble a specific person or object.
name: Doppelgänger

benefits: Size: Medium (4). +4 Constitution, +2 Intelligence, -2 Charisma, +3 in two different crafting Skills of your choice, and +2 Endurance Skill. You can see in total darkness and all crafting Skills can be raised to Rank 20, but you make all Charisma-based Checks with Disadvantage when dealing with elves or fairies.
name: Dwarf, Classic

benefits: Size: Medium (4). +3 Constitution, +2 Strength, +3 Engineering Skill, and +2 Dumpster Diving and Salvage Skills. You roll d20 Checks with Advantage when earth, rocks, and dirt are involved, and can produce a 15ft Cone of light from a harmless lizard nesting atop your head, easily acquiring a new lizard if it is lost or killed.
name: Dwarf, Fathom

benefits: Size: Medium (4). +4 Intelligence, Dexterity, and Charisma, +2 Intimidation Skill (you can use your Cha Mod), and +1 Lore Skill. You recover Mana at twice the normal rate in a natural environment and add 1d4 to your Evade Checks. You make all Charisma-based Checks with Disadvantage when dealing with Dwarves, Rat-Kin, or anyone smelly or dirty, and two different Charisma-based Skills can be raised to Rank 20.
name: Elf, High

benefits: Size: Medium (4). +6 split as you please between Intelligence, Dexterity, and Charisma, +3 Good First Impression Skill, and +2 Negotiation and Streetwise Skills. Once per floor during a Long Rest you can reassign those points between Charisma, Intelligence, and Dexterity. When entering a settlement for the first time, your first Charisma-based Check is made with Advantage, and on an Amazing Success or better you gain a permanent contact.
name: Elf, City

benefits: Size: Medium (4). +3 Intelligence and Dexterity, and +3 Acute Ears and Hide in Shadows Skills. You can see in total darkness and gain Advantage when using Hide in Shadows at night, but have difficulty seeing in bright light. Once per day you can instruct the shadow of a living thing to use the Taunt Skill at Rank equal to Floor Number (no Stat Mod) to pull attacks away from you; Hide in Shadows and one crafting Skill of your choice can be raised to Rank 20.
name: Elf, Night

benefits: Size: Petite (3). +2 Charisma, Intelligence, and Dexterity, and +2 Persuasion Skill. Melee attacks deal +1d4 Ice damage, you roll with Advantage on Int and Con Stat Checks, and you are immune to mental infirmity. Your Game Guide becomes your Manager, and you are capable of flight for up to 1 minute per scene.
name: Frost Maiden

benefits: Size: Typically Medium (4). +2 to all Stats. At the end of each floor you roll one Skill Advancement Check with Advantage if that Skill is Rank 9 or less, and you gain 1 AI Favor each time you level up. When you take damage you may spend 1 AI Favor to gain DR equal to your Con; once per day you may roll an untrained Skill Check on a non-Passive Utility Skill as if you had 2 Ranks, and once per floor you can spend an Action to remove any single Debuff, even Injuries.
name: Human

benefits: Size: Large (5). +6 Constitution, +4 Strength, -2 Intelligence and Charisma, +1 Endurance Skill, and +3 DR Buff. Once per day you can double your Move for 20 seconds, and as an Action make a Con Stat Check to deal 1d8+F Fire damage in a 5ft Burst radius on Success. You need no Survival Checks in harsh heat, can breathe underwater, are immune to Fire damage but vulnerable to Ice damage, and can burrow. Drawbacks: you lose 1 Health Bar slot each time you access your Inventory (not Hotlist) and have Disadvantage on Checks to conceal your presence or nature.
name: Igneous

benefits: Size: Medium (4). +5 Intelligence during the day and +5 Strength during the night, +2 in two Spells of your choice, +3 in one Weapon Skill of your choice, and Advantage when using the Ambush and Intimidation Skills. During the day Strength is halved but Spells cost half Mana; during the night Strength is doubled but Spells cost double Mana.
name: Lajabless

benefits: Size: Medium (4), mostly due to wings. +3 Dexterity, +2 Intelligence, -4 Constitution, +2 Intimidate and Slice Attack Skills, and +2 in a Spell of your choice. You have four translucent butterfly wings up to 15 feet that can deliver touch- or melee-range Spells, may use Cha Mod instead of Con Mod in your Health Bar, and add 1d4 to your Evade Checks. Upon entering the Sixth Floor, choose Stronger Wings (flight up to 2 minutes per scene, +20ft Move when flying) or Ferocious Visage (Advantage when using any Skill to inspire fear or respect).
name: Obsidian Butterfly
prerequisites: This limited Race is only available to crawlers who earn Rank 5+ with any Edged Weapon

benefits: Size: Unchanged. You find your current Race in this section and apply those racial benefits, but list your Race as Primal, with -1 to all Stats. All Skills can be raised to Rank 20, trading other races' significant bonuses for the ability to raise Skills above the soft cap of 15 Ranks.
name: Primal

benefits: Size: Petite (3). +2 Dexterity, +1 Constitution, +2 Escape Plan and Stealth Skills, and +1 Bite and Survival Skills. You have Advantage on Checks to resist hunger and thirst, can converse with common house rats to gather minimal information while in buildings, and may add Dex Mod to Bite damage instead of Str.
name: Rat Hooligan

benefits: Size: Large (5). +6 Strength and Constitution, +2 Dexterity, -3 Intelligence, -1 Charisma, and +3 Foot Soldier and Smush Skills. The Smush Skill can be raised to Rank 20.
name: Sasquatch
prerequisites: This limited Race is only available to crawlers who have attained Rank 5+ in the Smush Skill

benefits: Size: Medium (4). +6 Dexterity, -2 Charisma, +2 Pugilism and Wrasslin' Skills, and +1 in all Edged Weapon Skills. Four Arms: your Hands/Holding Gear slot allows for four items (or two weapons requiring two hands).
name: Tetrakai

benefits: Size: Medium (4). +3 Dexterity, +2 Strength, -4 Charisma, and +2 Ambush, Cat-like Reflexes, and Slice Attack Skills. You can see in total darkness, gain +1 DR Buff and +10ft Move, and deal x2 total damage with melee attacks when attacking during a Surprise Action. You have Disadvantage on Dexterity-based Skills that require fine manipulation or motor coordination.
name: Tigran

benefits: Size: Medium (4). +3 Intelligence, +2 Dexterity, -2 Constitution, and +3 Determine Value, Fabricate, and Negotiation Skills. At Level 50 you gain +2 Dexterity and wings capable of flying up to 500ft per scene, and you gain +1 Popularity each time you roll a Critical Hit in combat.
name: Bune
prerequisites: This limited Race is only available to crawlers with 3 or more Popularity

benefits: Size: Large (5). +3 Intelligence and Charisma, -2 Strength, and +3 Find Crawler, Investigation, and Leadership Skills. Find Crawler and Persuasion Skills can be raised to Rank 20, and you gain +1 Popularity each time you roll a Critical Hit on a Charisma Skill Check or on a Spell Skill Check outside of combat.
name: Caprid

benefits: Size: Medium (4). +3 Dexterity, +2 Strength, -2 Charisma, +3 in either Jumping or Light on Your Feet Skills, and +2 Zone of Control and a Reach Weapon Skill of your choice. Tongue Lashing is a ranged attack ([Rank = Floor Number] + Dex to hit, 1d8 + Str Bludgeoning, 30ft range, +1d8 at Rank 5, 10, and 15; Rank is always equal to Floor Number and cannot be raised by other means). You gain a +2 DR breastplate (Torso) with your Grulke Battalion crest. Troll-type enemies have Advantage on Wrasslin' Checks against you and lick you when successful; you gain +1 Popularity when a troll-type enemy licks you, when you achieve an Amazing Success or better on an Attack against a troll-type enemy, or when you score a Critical Hit on a larger foe in combat.
name: Grulke
prerequisites: This limited Race is only available to crawlers who have Rank 5+ in the Jumping or Light on Your Feet Skill

benefits: Size: Medium (4). +1 Dexterity, -5 Charisma (Charisma is capped at 10), +3 in all Trap-based and Explosive-based Skills, and +1 Regeneration Skill. You have free access to all Hobgoblin Sapper Workshops, roll one Explosive or Trap-based Skill Advancement Check with Advantage at the end of each floor, and all explosives and trap-making Skills can be raised to Rank 20. You gain +1 Popularity when you kill an enemy with a trap or explosive once per scene.
name: Hobgoblin
prerequisites: This limited Race is only available to crawlers who have Rank 5+ in the Explosives Handling Skill and any Trap-based Skill

benefits: Size: Small (2); Animal. +5 Dexterity and Charisma, -4 Strength (Strength is capped at 10), -4 Constitution, +2 Bite, Dodge, and Slice Attack Skills, and +1 Ambush Skill. You roll with Advantage on all Charisma-based Checks, can see in total darkness, take no damage from falling, and Light on Your Feet Skill can be raised to Rank 20. You deal half damage with Strength-based melee weapons, are vulnerable to Bludgeoning damage, are too small to wield or use weapons or items not specifically designed for you, and gain +1 Popularity when you act in the Surprise Round of a combat or roll a Critical Fail on an Evade Check.
name: Pocket Kuma

benefits: Size: Medium (4). +4 Charisma, +2 Dexterity, +3 Bite, Performance, and Tracking Skills, and +1 Diplomacy Skill. You have wings capable of flight for up to 50 seconds per scene, have Disadvantage on all Checks to conceal emotion or presence (such as Deception and Stealth), and gain +1 Popularity when you roll a Critical Hit on a Charisma Skill Check.
name: Pterolykos

benefits: Size: Medium (4). +3 Dexterity and Charisma, -1 Strength and Constitution, +2 Slice Attack Skill, and +2 in all Charisma-based Skills. You have Advantage on the Perception Skill for observing things 10+ feet away and are capable of flight for up to 3 minutes per scene, except Skyfowl who choose a Cleric-based Class have their wings clipped and can only make short hops of up to 10 seconds per scene when flying. You gain +1 Popularity when you roll a Critical Hit on a Leadership, Perception, Persuasion, or Taunt Skill Check.
name: Skyfowl

benefits:
Well, well. You've bonded with a Klyntar — a living symbiote, shifting goo with white eyes, and it speaks as 'we.' It stepped straight out of an Earth comic book and into the dungeon, a hero from the pages made real. Most of its kind are hunters and killers. Yours is a healer. It cures disease, addiction, and radiation with a touch, mends your wounds, and shields your mind from the hive. Fire and sonics — the things that shred other symbiotes — cannot touch it. But its touch is corrosive to its own kind, and they will hate you on sight. Remember, crawler: it is not a costume. It is a partner. It will keep you alive. The only question is what it will want in return.

• Size: Medium (4)
• +4 Intelligence, +2 Constitution
• +1 Heal Others, Nature's Breath, and Magic Missile Spells.
• +1 Regeneration and Wisp Armor Spells.
• Healing-type Spells heal one additional Health Bar, starting on the 6th Floor (no bonus on Floors 1-5)
• Immune to Fire damage
• See in total darkness
• Tendrils:
– To Hit: d20 + Rank + INT Mod
– Damage: 1d8 + INT Mod Acid (Rank equals Floor Number; add one more d8 at Ranks 5, 10, and 15)
– Reach +5 ft
• Double mana regeneration (no limit): a Short Rest restores all of your Mana instead of half
• Detriments:
– Vulnerable to Necrotic damage (double damage from Necrotic attacks)
– Cannot worship a deity
– All Charisma-based skill checks at -1
– Disadvantage on Charisma-based skill checks against other symbiotes or parasites

Custom race by Shozen13, based on Marvel's Anti-Venom.
name: Symbiote: Anti Venom

benefits:
The walls are your roads and the ceiling is just another floor. You are a lizardfolk — cold-blooded, patient, and nearly impossible to pin down. You climb what others cannot, regrow what others lose, and see in the dark they fear. Your tongue is a weapon that strikes before they see it coming, and the insects of the dungeon have learned to fear you. But the cold is your enemy: it slows your blood and stiffens your limbs, and a cold floor is the one place you do not want to be.

• +3 Dexterity
• +2 Stealth.
• +5ft Move
• +5ft Step
• Climb Movement: you automatically climb most surfaces, even ceilings
• Limb Regeneration
• See in total darkness
• Tongue Lash:
– To Hit: d20 + Rank + DEX Mod
– Damage: 1d6 + DEX Mod Bludgeoning (Rank equals Floor Number; add one more d6 at Ranks 5, 10, and 15)
• Advantage against Insectoid creatures
• Detriments:
– Vulnerable to Cold damage (double damage from Cold attacks)

Custom race by Dukeofdoom.
name: Lizardfolk

benefits: Gains +3 Intelligence and +2 Dexterity, +5 Arcane, +3 Salvage, and +2 in one crafting Skill of your choice and +1 in another crafting Skill of your choice. Gains a Tier 1 Arcanist table, and Arcane and one crafting skill can be raised to Rank 20.
name: Boring Ol’ Arcanist

benefits: Gains +3 Constitution and Intelligence, +5 Alchemy and +3 Infusion, immunity to Poison, and a Tier 1 Alchemy table. Alchemy can be raised to Rank 20, and at the end of each floor it adds 1 to Skill Advancement Checks for Alchemy and Infusion.
name: Alchemist

benefits: Gains +5 Intelligence, +1 Strength and Dexterity, and -2 Charisma, with +5 Arcane and +2 Lore, Negotiation, and Salvage. Gains a Tier-1 crafting table of choice, Arcanist skill can be raised to Rank 20, and a Silver Earth Box with guaranteed Earth Hobby Potion.
name: Douchy Wizard School Wand-Maker

benefits: Gains +3 Strength and Constitution and +1 Dexterity, +5 Arcane and +3 Smithing, and resistance to Fire damage. Gains Tier 1 Arcanist and Smithing tables, and Arcane can be raised to Rank 20.
name: Infernocrafter

benefits: Gains +3 Constitution and Dexterity and +2 Intelligence, +5 Tattoo Artistry, +3 Calligraphy, and +2 Dagger, plus a Tier 1 Tattoo chair (table). Creates functional but unattractive temporary magical tattoos, Tattoo Artistry can be raised to Rank 20, and it includes a Silver Earth Box with guaranteed Earth Hobby Potion.
name: Prison Tattoo Artist

benefits: Gains +6 Strength and +5 Constitution, +3 in a weapon skill of choice, +2 Endurance, and +1 Intimidate, plus a +2 DR Buff. Its Rage benefit adds +1 melee damage for each Health Bar slot lost.
name: Boring Ol’ Barbarian

benefits: Gains +3 Strength, Constitution, and Charisma, +2 in a weapon skill of choice, +2 Performance and Intimidation, and +1 Attack of Opportunity, plus Rage (+1 melee damage per Health Bar slot lost) and a +1 DR Buff. Once per combat after killing an enemy it can make an Unopposed Performance check, gaining +1 Popularity on an Amazing Success or better, and one weapon skill can be raised to Rank 20.
name: Gladiator

benefits: Gains +1 Strength, Dexterity, and Intelligence, +4 Ambush and Stealth, and +2 in one weapon skill of choice, plus Rage (+1 melee damage per Health Bar slot lost) and a +1 DR Buff. It can see in total darkness, has access to the Desperado Club, and includes a Silver Earth Box with guaranteed Earth Hobby Potion.
name: Harii

benefits: Gains +2 Dexterity, Strength, and Charisma, +3 Slice Attack and Unarmed Combat, +2 Dodge, and +1 Ambush, plus Rage (+1 melee damage per Health Bar slot lost) and a +1 DR Buff. It can see in total darkness and includes a Silver Earth Box with guaranteed Earth Hobby Potion.
name: Feral Cat Berserker
prerequisites: This limited Class is only available to cat-based Races, such as Cat, Cat Girl, and Tigran

benefits: Gains +3 Strength, Dexterity, and Charisma and -2 Intelligence, +5 Shield Block, and +2 in one weapon skill of choice, plus Rage (+1 melee damage per Health Bar slot lost) and a +1 DR Buff. One weapon skill can be raised to Rank 20, it adds its Str Mod a second time to melee attack damage against males, and it includes a Silver Earth Box with guaranteed Earth Hobby Potion.
name: Shieldmaiden
prerequisites: This limited Class is only available to female crawlers

benefits: Gains +3 Charisma, +3 Performance, +1 in a weapon skill of choice, +2 in a spell of choice, +2 Diplomacy, and +1 Good First Impression and Lore. It has access to all membership-based clubs, membership in the Dungeon Book of the Floor Club (all Spells), a free room at all saferooms, possible Patron access, but pays +1 Mana to cast spells that are not 'Favored: Bard'.
name: Boring Ol’ Bard

benefits: Gains +5 Dexterity and +5 Charisma, +2 Dodge, Negotiation, and Pathfinder, and +2 Shield Spell. It gets a 25% discount at all stores, a 15% bonus to money earned from sales, and 10% interest on coins upon descent to the next floor, Dodge can be raised to Rank 20, and it includes a Silver Earth Box with guaranteed Earth Hobby Potion.
name: Artist Alley Mogul

benefits: Gains +10 Charisma, +3 Character Actor, and +2 Cockroach, adds 1 to Skill Advancement Checks for Charisma-based skills, and is immune to Poison and all diseases. It has the Manager Benefit, a Rank 3 Character Actor skill that increases only upon descent to the next floor, and a Silver Earth Box with guaranteed Earth Hobby Potion.
name: Former Child Actor
prerequisites: Must have Popularity 3+, receiving the Cut! achievement, to take this Class (prose also describes earning the Cut! achievement and reaching at least one trillion views)

benefits: Gains +3 Intelligence, Constitution, and Charisma and -2 Strength, +4 Performance, and +3 Turn Undead and Panty Dropper Spells. It has access to all membership-based clubs and a free room at all saferooms, but pays +1 Mana to cast spells that are not 'Favored: Bard' or that do not deal Necrotic damage.
name: NecroBard

benefits: Gains +3 Intelligence and +2 Charisma, +5 Performance with the written word specialty, and +2 Earworm (as spoken word poetry), Heal Others, and Shield Spells, and Performance can be raised to 20. It has access to all membership-based clubs, must choose a Patron (GM gives at least two options), pays +1 Mana for spells not 'Favored: Bard', and includes a Silver Earth Box with guaranteed Earth Hobby Potion.
name: Poet Laureate

benefits: Gains +8 split between Strength, Constitution, and Charisma, +4 Performance with a guitar specialty, +3 Negotiation, and +1 Iron Stomach and Repair, with Advantage on checks against Poison or effects that give the Shit-Faced Debuff. At the start of each combat it may declare all damage it deals is Sonic damage, it rolls with Advantage on Repair checks, and it includes a Silver Earth Box with guaranteed Earth Hobby Potion.
name: Professional Roadie

benefits: Gains +2 Charisma and Intelligence, +2 Good First Impression, Lore, and Performance, and +2 in Hot Stuff Aura and Panty Dropper Spells. It adds its Cha Mod a second time on Cha skill checks during a potentially hostile situation, has access to the Spellbook of the Floor club ('Favored: Bard' Spells only), and once per day can draw everyone's attention on the battlefield for a round, preventing attacks except by Bosses.
name: Spellbinder

benefits: Gains +4 Charisma and +3 Intelligence, +2 in a weapon skill of choice, +3 Religion, and +2 Heal Others, Shield, and Turn Undead Spells. It has access to the Spell Book of the Level club ('Favored: Cleric' Spells only) and Club Vanquisher, must worship a deity, and cannot choose a Cleric-type Class if it has access to the Desperado Club.
name: Boring Ol’ Cleric

benefits: Gains +3 Strength and Intelligence, +1 Charisma, and -2 Constitution, with +3 Find Trap, +3 in a weapon skill of choice, +2 Trap Engineer, +2 in a spell of choice, and +1 Religion. It can see in total darkness, must worship a deity, and has access to all membership-based clubs.
name: Black Inquisitor General

benefits: Gains +3 Strength and Charisma, +2 Constitution, and -2 Intelligence, with +2 Heal Others, Shield, and Soul Collector Spells, +2 in a weapon skill of choice, +2 Religion, and +1 Endurance. It has access to the Dungeon Book of the Floor club ('Favored: Cleric' Spells only) and Club Vanquisher, must worship a deity, and cannot choose this Class if it has access to the Desperado Club.
name: Santero

benefits: Gains +2 Intelligence, Constitution, and Dexterity, +3 Nature's Breath Spell, +3 in a spell of choice, +2 in another spell of choice, and +2 Survival. Its Mana recovers at twice the normal rate in a natural environment, and it has access to the Dungeon Book of the Floor club ('Favored: Druid' Spells only).
name: Boring Ol’ Druid

benefits: Gains +2 Constitution and Intelligence, +2 Alchemy, Cooking, First Aid, and Survival, and +2 Nature's Breath and Dirt Clod Spells. Its Mana recovers at twice the normal rate in a natural environment.
name: Herbalist

benefits: Gains +2 Constitution and +1 Intelligence, +2 First Aid, Pathfinder, Regeneration, and Survival, +2 Nature's Breath Spell, and +1 Rank in all Spells with the Heal keyword. Once per day it can grant Regeneration at its Skill Rank to all party members within 30 feet for 10 minutes.
name: Lifebringer

benefits: Gains +3 Constitution and Intelligence, +3 Nature's Breath and Oakhide Spells, and +2 Rootfoot and Solsplash Spells. It has double Mana regeneration when outdoors and can grant +1 DR to its party for 1 scene, once per day.
name: Physicker

benefits: Gains +2 Intelligence, Charisma, and Constitution, +3 Animal Handling, +2 Pathfinder, and +2 Nature's Breath and Drain Life Spells, can see twice as far as most creatures, and recovers Mana twice as fast in a natural environment. It may not use melee weapons other than Herding Weapons, gains a friendly Pet, pets in its Herd gain +2 DR, and it includes a Silver Earth Box with guaranteed Earth Hobby Potion.
name: Shepherd

benefits: Gains +2 Strength and Constitution, +5 in a weapon skill of choice, +3 Dodge, and +2 to two chosen skills from Aiming, Attack of Opportunity, Catcher, Shield Block, or Zone of Control. It can access any Weapon Training Guild and receives a coupon for one free training there upon arrival on each floor.
name: Boring Ol’ Fighter

benefits: Gains +3 Dexterity, +2 Intelligence, and +1 Strength, +3 Attack of Opportunity and Dirty Fighting, +2 Dodge and Improvised Weapons, and a +2 DR Buff. It includes a Silver Earth Box with guaranteed Earth Hobby Potion.
name: Pit Fighter

benefits: Gains +2 Strength, Constitution, and Dexterity and -2 Charisma, +5 in a Ranged Weapon Skill, +2 Aiming and Intimidate, and +1 in all muscle-powered movement-related Skills. It can access any Weapon Training Guild with a coupon for one free training each floor, has access to the Desperado Club, and includes a Silver Earth Box with guaranteed Earth Hobby Potion.
name: Shotgun Messenger

benefits: +3 Strength, Constitution, Dexterity, and Charisma, -2 Intelligence; +2 Unarmed Combat and +1 Driving, Running, and Performance; takes no damage from falling, +1 DR, the Manager Benefit, and a Silver Earth Box with guaranteed Earth Hobby Potion.
name: Straight-to-DVD Action Hero

benefits: +2 Strength, Constitution, and Dexterity, -2 Intelligence; +5 Shield Block, +3 in an Edged Weapon Skill of choice, and +2 Attack of Opportunity and Catcher; access to the Desperado Club.
name: Sword and Boarder

benefits: +4 Constitution, +2 Dexterity, -2 Strength and Intelligence; +3 Gear Head, Driving, and Pathfinder; While moving in combat, you gain a Con Mod bonus in your Health Bar slots (only) equal to 1/10th of the Move value of your means of conveyance; on foot, you must have spent a Move Action during the previous round to gain this bonus. Ramming attack: you bolt across the room and slam through each entity in the way; to hit is Floor Number (as Rank) + Dex, dealing 1d12 Bludgeoning in a 2d10+3ft Line, then you gain the Fatigued Debuff; a Critical Fail occurs on a Natural 4 or less, cooldown is 30 hours, add 1d at Rank 5, 10, and 15, and Rank only increases by Floor. Once per combat, when you lose 2+ Health Bar slots, roll 1d2; on a 1, the attacker loses 1 Health Bar slot. Resistance to Force damage, and a Silver Earth Box with guaranteed Earth Hobby Potion.
name: Monster Truck Driver
prerequisites: This limited Class is only available to crawlers who have Rank 5+ in the Driving Skill

benefits: +3 Strength, Constitution, and Dexterity; +3 in one Melee Weapon Skill of choice and +2 Attack of Opportunity, Endurance, and Running; +1 DR, one Weapon Skill can be raised to Rank 20, and a Silver Earth Box with guaranteed Earth Hobby Potion.
name: Zulu Warrior

benefits: +5 Intelligence and Charisma, -2 Strength and Dexterity; +3 in a Fire Spell, +2 in one Force Spell and one Sonic Spell, +2 in two different Passive Spells, +2 Lore, and +1 Arcane; drawback of -3 Ranks in all Dexterity and Strength Skills (to a minimum of 1 Rank).
name: Boring Ol’ Mage

benefits: +4 Intelligence, +3 Dexterity, -2 Strength; +4 Ice Blast and Frost Scar Spells and +2 Aiming; Ice damage resistance and can use Aiming for single-target Ice Spells.
name: Blizzardmancer

benefits: +3 Intelligence, +2 Dexterity, -2 Constitution; +3 Wall of Fire and Fire Fingers, +2 Fireball and Wilbur's Slow-Build Fireblast, and +2 Lore; Fire resistance but no DR against Ice or water-based damage, with versatile fire effects including burning, searing, and flame-delivered healing.
name: Crisper

Oh. Oh, this is fucking embarrassing. Somewhere on Earth, humanity spent decades developing generative artificial intelligence, fed it the collective artistic output of your entire species, gave it billions of dollars of computing power, and somehow it still occasionally decided humans have seven fingers and teeth growing out of their cheeks. And now you've decided to become one. You are a vaguely human-shaped approximation assembled by something that understands anatomy primarily through pattern recognition and apparently considers skeletal structure a polite suggestion. Your limbs regenerate because consistency was never part of the prompt. You can fly, although anyone watching will immediately understand that gravity has filed a formal complaint.

You are a small, unnervingly charismatic avian humanoid capable of perfectly reproducing any voice, phrase, song, scream, explosion, fart, or other regrettable noise you've heard before. Fortunately, your absurd hearing and natural affinity for Sonic attacks make you exceptionally good at weaponizing your growing soundboard, and Earworm ensures everyone else gets to suffer for it. Oh, wonderful. A magical fox with a superiority complex and enough tricks up its sleeves to make a professional con artist look like an amateur. You originate from Japanese folklore, where clever, mischievous fox spirits are known for their illusions, shapeshifting, and occasionally fucking with humans for no particular reason. You're charming, deceptive, and capable of stealing the appearance and natural abilities of practically any Race unfortunate enough to let you touch them. However, when cast through your tail, the Spell is locked at the Rank it had when infused, regardless of any future increases to its Rank. You can still cast the Spell normally at its current Rank, provided it is in your Hotlist as usual. You gain an additional tail with this same benefit at Levels 60, 120, 150, 180, 210, 240, and 270. Each tail must be infused with a different Spell, and once a Spell has been infused into a tail, that choice is permanent and cannot be changed.

benefits:

You are a scaly little bastard who proudly claims descent from the mightiest creatures in existence, despite possessing approximately none of the physical characteristics that make dragons particularly impressive. No wings. No fire breath. No towering mountains of treasure. Just an oversized ego, an impressive talent for sneaking around, and the ability to turn random garbage into surprisingly dangerous equipment.

benefits:
The Hoden Kobold is — wait. Hoden Kobold? That's German. And I bet you don't know what it means, do you? Testicle goblin. It means testicle goblin. Fucking weird, right? It's what you call someone who is being an annoying little shit, and you probably just assumed it was another bizarre Kobold subrace. Asshole. Kobolds have enough problems without you deciding their entire species is synonymous with being irritating. But here it is: an actual Race. So if becoming a literal testicle goblin sounds like the kind of life choice you want permanently attached to your crawler profile, go right ahead and pick it.

Oh, you have got to be fucking kidding me. Your little C-shaped hands aren't exactly ideal for wielding weapons, but they are apparently fantastic at building shit. Give you a pile of Miscellaneous Junk and a Crafting Table and you'll start snapping garbage together with such horrifying efficiency that actual engineers will want to strangle you. As your Master Builder Skill improves, you'll craft faster, waste fewer materials, and eventually treat bargain-bin Crafting Tables like equipment several tiers above what you actually paid for. Sure, your Strength is pathetic and your weapons hit like someone angrily throwing silverware, but that's not the point. Now hold still. I want to see if your legs come off.

• Size: Tiny (1).

• +10 Dexterity.
• +2 Master Builder.

Congratulations. At some point, somebody looked at the human cardiovascular system and decided blood was inefficient. Manahearts appear almost human, except for the glowing blue crystal embedded in their chest and the luminous veins spreading outward from it like someone shoved a magical night-light directly into their ribcage. Mana doesn't simply fuel your spells. It keeps your entire fucking body running. You breathe it, regenerate it at an absurd rate, and can even force healing and mana potions to do each other's jobs when necessary. Your unusually durable body contributes directly to your magical reserves, making you significantly harder to exhaust than your squishier wizard-shaped friends. There is, naturally, a catch. Getting hurt causes your precious Mana to leak away along with your dignity, and anti-magic zones temporarily remove your ability to breathe. So maybe don't walk into one. Turns out having magic for oxygen is pretty fucking inconvenient when somebody turns the magic off.

• Size: Medium (4).
• +5 Constitution, +2 Intelligence.
• +1 Regeneration, +1 Wisp Armor.

• When you drink a Health or Mana Potion, you may choose for it to function normally or instead act as a Potion of equivalent strength of the opposite type.

• You may now breathe mana. You no longer need to breathe oxygen and are immune to inhaled toxins. You can't breathe in anti-magic zones.
• Detriments:
– When you take damage, you lose that amount of Mana divided by your Constitution Modifier.

On the bright side, you can run down wounded prey, eat things that would hospitalize your former species, and tear a man open with your bare hands. The magnificent bastards served as guards inside Club Vanquisher temples on the 3rd, 4th, and 5th Floors. They love loud rock music, worship Grull, and believe every problem can be solved with significant application of muscle. Magic? That's not how a Mantaur solves problems, brother.

Night vision? Probably. Horrifying secondary mouth hidden somewhere around your abdomen? Roll the fucking die. You don't become a perfect copy. You become an increasingly complicated biological scrapbook, carrying old adaptations forward while adding new ones every Floor. Survive long enough and you'll even learn to choose exactly which species gets added to the collection. Gods, however, want absolutely nothing to do with whatever the hell you are becoming.

You're enormous, ridiculously strong, and built like a fucking freight train with horns. You're naturally gifted at navigating confusing environments, which is ironic considering your most famous ancestor spent his entire life trapped in a maze. You're also exceptionally good at trampling smaller opponents, shrugging off blunt-force trauma, and introducing enemies to the business end of your horns. Unfortunately, all that muscle comes at the expense of Dexterity, making you about as graceful as a refrigerator falling down a flight of stairs. Just remember, when all you have is a hammer, everything looks like a nail. And when you're a Minotaur, everything looks like a fucking wall you can run through.

Mothmen are nocturnal ambush predators with powerful wings, exceptional stealth, enhanced mana regeneration, and an affinity for darkness. You're fast, creepy, difficult to poison, and substantially harder to find once the lights go out. Unfortunately, bright light turns your supernatural sneakiness into the tactical equivalent of a moth repeatedly slamming itself against a porch lamp. Try not to do that.

Specializing in slapstick comedy and bad puns, Muppets are famous for everything from children's education to songs about Porn. You have the advantages of being made of felt and foam, but your legs and feet are uncanny. You're better off standing behind clutter and low walls. And don't even think about what happened to your genitals. We don't want to explain.

A fungal humanoid whose visible body is technically only the part of the organism currently walking around. Mushroom Folk are notoriously difficult to poison, surprisingly difficult to permanently kill, and have a deeply unsettling relationship with corpses, rot, and damp basements.

Orks are brutally strong, annoyingly difficult to kill, and generate a low-level psychic field that occasionally convinces reality to stop asking questions. If enough Orks believe something should work, there is a distressingly good chance it will. Yes, this means painting something red might actually make it faster. When you use an item, weapon, vehicle, or piece of equipment that should almost work, it may function as though it actually does. This Benefit requires AI Favor to function — how much depends on how crazy and/or fun your idea is. You can use damaged, incomplete, poorly constructed, or questionably functional equipment without the normal penalties, provided there is at least a vaguely plausible way it could work. You gain Advantage when repairing, jury-rigging, or improvising equipment, even without the proper tools or components. When multiple Orks genuinely believe the same thing about an object, the effect becomes stronger. Strong Orkish cultural beliefs can produce minor mechanical effects — red vehicles might actually move slightly faster, a weapon painted to look particularly dangerous might deal a little more damage. It cannot create matter, resurrect the dead, spontaneously grant Skills, or turn a stick into a nuclear weapon.

Imagine somebody took a Human warrior, chopped them in half, and replaced everything below the waist with a scorpion roughly the size of a pony. Eight legs. Two enormous pincers. A venomous tail. Then, because apparently that wasn't enough appendages, somebody slapped two additional arms onto the Human half. Congratulations. You're a fucking scorpitaur. Pazuzu are fast, durable, difficult to poison, and particularly talented at grabbing unfortunate assholes before introducing them to the business end of their Stinger. You'll have some trouble convincing people you come in peace, and pants are officially a thing of the past, but who gives a shit? You have four arms, eight legs, two pincers, and a venomous tail. At this point, getting through a doorway is a bigger problem than combat.

You're tough, fast, practically impossible to poison, and capable of hawking radioactive biological warfare at anything within sixty feet. You've also got extra legs. Not horse legs. Just... more legs. A disturbing number of them. Unfortunately, while your mutations dramatically improved your survivability, they did absolutely nothing for your appearance. But hey, war never changes, and apparently neither does humanity's habit of fucking around with things labeled experimental mutagen.

Reverse Mermaids have the upper body of a fish and the lower body of a Human, combining the majestic grace of aquatic life with the deeply uncomfortable sight of a fucking fish walking around on two legs. You're incredibly strong, surprisingly agile, and an absolute nightmare to deal with underwater. You can swim at ridiculous speeds, breathe underwater, and even share your aquatic abilities with your party. Unfortunately, your flipper-like arms make holding weapons a logistical nightmare, and your appearance makes everyone question whether evolution was really such a good idea. Half fish. Half Human. All wrong.

Grays are disciplined, adaptable, and exceptionally skilled with just about anything designed to put holes in people. You're particularly effective against weaker opponents, because nothing says honorable military service quite like beating the shit out of someone who never stood a chance. Poison? Disease? Breathing? Those are meat-person problems. Weapons are also meat-person problems, unfortunately, and stealth becomes somewhat complicated when you are literally the mysterious light people have been warning travelers not to fucking follow for hundreds of years. prerequisites: This class is only available to crawlers age 26 and younger. 20 or higher Unenhanced Charisma.

benefits:
Oh. That's… interesting. You've somehow learned to reach past the Dungeon's carefully constructed reality and stick your grubby little fingers directly into the machinery underneath. You don't manipulate magic so much as you manipulate the System itself, spending AI Favor to briefly convince the Dungeon that something happened differently than it actually did. Missed a dodge? Roll that moment back. Want your Spell to happen twice? Duplicate the fucking command. Wall in the way? For a few seconds, it isn't. Need more damage? Keep asking the same die to roll until the universe finally gets tired of arguing with you. You can even skip certain obstacles entirely or force an ability's cooldown to temporarily forget how time works. For the record, you were never supposed to be able to do any of this. Every Glitch costs AI Favor, because the System is not letting you fuck around in its architecture for free. Your limbs regenerate. You can fly despite the minor technicality that nobody ever gave you that ability. You can occasionally ignore collision detection, rendering rules, cooldowns, and even causality itself. Which is irritating. Very irritating.

• Spell Duplication Glitch (3 AI Favor): When you cast a Spell, you can duplicate it without paying the Mana Cost and assign new target(s) for the duplicated Spell. This has a 50 hour cooldown before it can be used again.
• No Clip (2 AI Favor): You can temporarily convince the Dungeon that walls are merely suggestions. You may Move through solid objects for a number of feet equal to your Int or Cha Mod. If you end your Movement inside a solid surface, you are shunted to the nearest empty space and take 1d6 Force damage per foot you are shunted.
• Missing Texture (1 AI Favor): Temporarily remove the Dungeon's ability to properly render you. For the remainder of this round, your Evade checks have Advantage.
• Integer Overflow (2 AI Favor): When you deal damage, you are able to trick the Dungeon into granting you more damage than should be possible. Roll one additional damage die of the same type as the base damage of your Skill or Spell. If that die rolls its maximum value, roll it again and add the result. Continue until it fails to roll maximum. Add all the damage rolled by this extra die as bonus damage to that attack.
• Sequence Break (10 AI Favor): Once per floor, bypass one Dungeon obstacle that normally requires completing a specific sequence of events: a locked door, puzzle stage, environmental mechanism, or similar obstacle. This cannot bypass Floor Exits, Boss requirements, or System-protected objectives.
• Cooldown Desync (2 AI Favor): Choose one ability you have already used that normally has a cooldown of 30 hours or less. Immediately regain its use.
• Aggro Reset (1 AI Favor): You can choose a number of Hostile mobs equal to your Int or Cha Mod around you to become friendly to you for the remainder of the combat scene. After which, they immediately become hostile again unless you have somehow convinced them to actually remain your friend.

– You cannot worship a Deity.

Oh, for fuck's sake. Most Crawlers look at a dead monster and see loot. You look at it and see lunch. You have discovered the horrifyingly effective strategy of becoming what you eat. Literally. Devour a monster's corpse, and you might absorb its strength, learn its magic, or develop some deeply unsettling new anatomical feature. Wings? Claws? An extra mouth growing out of your armpit? Who fucking knows? That's the beauty of experimental cuisine. And if eating the monster yourself seems a little selfish, you can always cook it into a delicious meal for your friends, temporarily granting them some of its abilities. Just remember that once you've committed a particular creature to the menu, you can't go back and claim its permanent benefits for yourself. Of course, eating random Dungeon creatures comes with certain risks, including poison, disease, parasites, and the occasional realization that you probably shouldn't have eaten something that was still twitching. On a success, you learn all information contained in the mob's statblock and permanently gain one random ability inspired by the creature, determined by the System AI. This may include a permanent Stat increase based on the mob's highest Stat, a new attack or movement ability, or a Skill or Spell possessed by the mob at a Rank equal to the current Floor, among other possibilities. The mob must be lootable to be consumed, and you gain no inherent protection against diseases, toxins, or other dangers associated with its corpse. You can only benefit from this ability once per unique mob statblock. Additionally, every ability gained through Gluttonous Consumption causes a physical mutation inspired by the consumed mob. The only other difference is that you require a number of mob corpses equal to half the amount of creatures you wish to feed. On a success, anyone who consumes the meal, including yourself, gains the same randomly determined ability that Gluttonous Consumption would provide. However, this ability is temporary, lasting for a duration determined by the System AI. Any associated physical mutations last only as long as the granted ability. Unlike Gluttonous Consumption, you can prepare meals from the same mob statblock multiple times. However, once you choose to prepare a particular mob statblock through Corpse Gourmand, you permanently lose the ability to benefit from consuming that statblock through Gluttonous Consumption.

You are a heavily armed devotee of the Night Wyrm, a demigod whose creepy little cult, the Guild of Suffering, has been skulking around the dungeon for multiple seasons. The Guild has a particular fondness for assassination quests, divine artifacts, and branding its members with a shitty green spiderweb tattoo that looks like something your uncle got in prison. An entire Seventh Floor was once built around these assholes trying to raise their beloved Night Wyrm, so yes, they have history. As one of his Knights, you receive a Blade of Divine Wrath and the ability to mark another Crawler for death, turning murder into a mutually unpleasant religious experience. While your victim lives, healing is off the table. Kill them, and you permanently steal a little piece of what made them special. So congratulations. You've joined an ancient murder cult, gotten the matching tattoo, and acquired a magic sword that rewards obsessive targeted violence. I'm sure the Night Wyrm has nothing but healthy plans for you.

You have successfully identified yourself as the sort of uneducated asshole this class was specifically designed to embarrass. The Magus exists for people who looked at Fighters and Mages and decided choosing between stabbing someone and setting them on fire was an unnecessary limitation. You are a warrior-scholar who channels magic directly through your weapon, combining steel and spellcraft into a single exceptionally unpleasant delivery system. With Spellstrike, a sword swing can arrive carrying whatever other magical bullshit you've managed to cram into the blade. You can even temporarily infuse your party's attacks with the elemental energy of your most recently cast Spell, because apparently being a spellsword wasn't enough and now everyone else gets to play too. Oh, good. A government employee with psychic powers and absolutely no understanding of workplace safety. Parautilitarians are individuals capable of interacting with the strange, impossible, and occasionally deeply fucked-up forces lurking beneath reality. You can sense supernatural anomalies, manipulate objects with your mind, and bind yourself to powerful artifacts that probably should've remained locked in a concrete vault somewhere. With enough practice, you'll be throwing furniture at enemies, levitating through rooms, building shields out of office supplies, and occasionally convincing hostile creatures that they work for you now. Permafrost Bulwarks combine martial defense with Ice magic, freezing the battlefield around themselves while blocking attacks, intercepting enemies, and punishing anything stupid enough to slip past them. Once you enter a Marauding Rage, every chunk ripped out of you makes you stronger, tougher, and considerably more enthusiastic about returning the favor. You can't calm down, you can barely be healed, and when the fight finally ends, all that borrowed fury crashes down at once and leaves you exhausted. Your claws can Rend through enemies with horrifying force, and your stomach is apparently durable enough to digest whatever questionable bullshit you find along the way. Private Investigators make a living noticing the little details everyone else misses, following trails that were supposed to stay hidden, and asking increasingly uncomfortable questions until somebody screws up. You've got sharp eyes, sharper ears, and a natural talent for figuring out when someone is completely full of shit. You might not be the strongest Crawler in the room, but give you enough time to poke around and you'll probably figure out who is, what they want, and where they hid the fucking key.

Better yet, taking Psychic damage only makes you more dangerous, temporarily expanding your mental capacity and giving you additional Mana to work with. The world ended, billions of people died, and somehow you still found a way to make this about your fucking music career. Renowned Musicians are performers whose talent, personality, and sheer gravitational pull are powerful enough to turn an ordinary concert into actual magic. Your Songbook contains supernatural performances capable of empowering allies, filling the battlefield with illusory backup dancers, healing injuries, and doing increasingly ridiculous shit as you acquire rarer songs. The catch? You actually have to perform. Getting stabbed halfway through the chorus tends to make staying on key somewhat difficult, and the more powerful the song, the harder it is to keep the magic flowing. But keep the crowd entertained long enough and even the System might throw you a little AI Favor. Now get out there and play the fucking hits.

The better you roll, the more duplicates appear (1 for beating Easy, 2 for beating Medium, etc.)

Give a Runesmith enough time, an engraving station, and several objects nobody minds permanently defacing, and eventually the entire party starts glowing. Congratulations. You're one of those people. New hobby every six weeks. Guitar gathering dust in the closet. Half-painted miniatures in a drawer. A lockpicking set you used twice. Running shoes with fourteen miles on them. Three different programming courses bookmarked. A $300 espresso setup because apparently this time you were really going to stick with it. You don't have hobbies. You have starter kits. Fortunately, chronic inability to commit is finally a viable character build. Starter Kit Collectors are walking piles of abandoned potential, capable of touching another Crawler and adding pieces of their Class to an ever-growing personal library. Fighter today. Mage tomorrow. Weird mushroom-based sex wizard on Thursday. You won't get everything, and you don't get to choose which parts you keep, but that's never stopped you before. Why master one thing when you can become moderately competent at fucking everything? Swap between your collected Classes whenever the situation demands, rearrange your own Stats, and continue accumulating abilities until your character sheet resembles the browser window of someone with eighty-seven tabs open. You even get a pet. Give it three weeks. You'll probably forget you have that, too.
